q: What is the carbon footprint of the Bargarh rice mill cluster, given most energy is husk?
title: Bargarh rice mills: husk, power and CO2
short: The fossil part is grid power: about 33,750 t CO2 a year from 50 million kWh. TERI's 2014-15 profile of Bargarh's 95 mills also counts 241,445 t of husk, 94% of their energy. Husk CO2 is biogenic and reported separately; its methane and nitrous oxide belong in Scope 1.
audience: Parboiled rice mills in Bargarh district, Odisha, milling paddy for the state PDS

ul: 67 small mills at 2 tph: 3,43,855 t of rice a year.
19 medium mills at 4 tph: 1,95,022 t. 9 large mills at 10 tph: 2,30,947 t.
About 7.7 lakh t of rice from about 1.2 million t of paddy, all parboiled, mostly for the state's public distribution system.
Husk is about 23% of paddy; about 90% is burnt in the mill's own boiler and the rest sold.

sections.h: A typical mill in a year
ul: 2 tph: 1,610 t of husk and 3,33,590 kWh.
4 tph: 3,219 t of husk and 6,67,181 kWh.
10 tph: 8,048 t of husk and 16,67,952 kWh. Three such mills run 2 MW of cogeneration for their own use.

ol: Scope 2: grid kWh x 0.675 kg CO2. This is the number most buyers and lenders compare.
Scope 1: methane and nitrous oxide from burning husk, small but real.
Biogenic CO2 from husk: reported separately, outside the scopes, never added to the total.

p: The profile prints 4,903 t CO2 for the cluster without showing its factor. Work from your own kWh instead: it is the line you can prove with bills.

example.title: Cluster and per tonne (estimate)
lines: Grid: 50 million kWh x 0.675 kg = 33,750 t CO2
Per tonne of rice: 50 million kWh / 7.70 lakh t = 65 kWh = 44 kg CO2
Small mill: 3,33,590 kWh x 0.675 kg = 225 t CO2 a year
Husk: 72,433 toe = 3,033 TJ x 100 t CO2 per TJ = about 303,000 t biogenic CO2
Husk methane and nitrous oxide: 3,033 TJ x (30 kg x 27 + 4 kg x 273) = about 5,800 t CO2e, Scope 1
example.note: Quantities from TERI's Bargarh profile. IPCC 2006 defaults for solid biomass (100 t CO2, 30 kg CH4, 4 kg N2O per TJ), AR6 GWPs, CEA FY 2025-26 grid factor.

senseible: Senseible reads your electricity bills into monthly records with the CEA factor for each bill's year, which is the fossil line your carbon number per tonne of rice rests on.

sources.label: TERI, Cluster profile: Bargarh rice mills (2014-15 data)
CEA, CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector (grid factor 0.675 kg CO2 per kWh, FY 2025-26)
IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Volume 2 Energy (fuel emission factors)
IPCC AR6 Working Group I (global warming potentials)
